translations.title.home: WinDict · Look up and translate any word on Windows
translations.desc.start: How to install WinDict on Windows, or run it without installing, and look up your first word.
translations.desc.lookup: Look up any word on Windows with Alt+D: definitions, similar and opposite words, pronunciation, pinned cards and more.
translations.desc.translate: Translate a word, a phrase or a whole passage on Windows with Alt+T, between 22 languages.
translations.desc.keys: Every keyboard shortcut in WinDict, from anywhere in Windows and on the card.
translations.desc.above: How WinDict shows its card on top of the Windows Start menu and Search, with UI access.
translations.desc.settings: Every setting in WinDict, and its settings file.
translations.desc.dicts: Where WinDict's definitions and translations come from, and what it sends over the network.
translations.desc.build: How to build WinDict and its setup from source, with Rust and Inno Setup.
translations.footer.tagline: Look up and translate any word on Windows, right where you read it.

translations.nav.label: Main
translations.docs.above.title: Above the Start menu
translations.docs.above.lead: Look up words in Start and Search, with the card on top of them.
translations.home.start.shotAlt: WinDict's “Look up a word” box open above the Windows Start menu
translations.docs.above.why: Windows keeps Start and Search above every ordinary window, so by default WinDict closes them before showing a definition. To have the card appear on top of them instead, WinDict needs “UI access”, which Windows only grants to signed apps installed in a protected folder.
translations.docs.above.on.title: Turning it on
translations.docs.above.on.1: Install WinDict with {$START_LINK}the setup{$CLOSE_LINK}. Only the copy the setup installs can have UI access, so the downloaded {$START_TAG_CODE}WinDict-<version>.exe{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} doesn't show the switch.
translations.docs.above.on.2: Use the {$START_TAG_STRONG}Show above Start{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} switch: on the introduction's {$START_TAG_STRONG}Show the card above Start{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} step, or in the settings under {$START_TAG_STRONG}General{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}.
translations.docs.above.on.3: Windows asks for permission, then WinDict restarts with UI access.
translations.docs.above.off: Turn the switch off to go back.
translations.docs.above.how.title: How it works
translations.docs.above.how.1: The setup installs a second build of WinDict that asks for UI access, but leaves it unsigned. The switch runs {$START_TAG_CODE}uiaccess.ps1{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, which creates a certificate that's trusted on this machine only, signs that build with it and restarts WinDict.
translations.docs.above.how.2: The certificate's private key is deleted right after signing, so it can't be used to sign anything else. Updates sign the new version the same way. Turning UI access off removes the certificate, and uninstalling WinDict does that too.
translations.docs.above.how.3: The script can also be run by hand, from an administrator PowerShell:
translations.docs.above.how.4: Use {$START_TAG_CODE}-Disable -Restart{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} instead to turn UI access off.
translations.docs.above.snip.title: Print Screen
translations.docs.above.snip.text: With UI access, Windows doesn't hear Print Screen pressed over WinDict's windows, so WinDict opens Snipping Tool itself, as Windows would have, if Print Screen is set to open it.
translations.docs.build.title: Building from source
translations.docs.build.lead: WinDict is written in Rust, against the native Windows APIs. Building it needs Windows and a Rust toolchain, 1.88 or newer.
translations.docs.build.setup.title: Building the setup
translations.docs.build.setup.text: The installer is built with {$START_LINK}Inno Setup{$CLOSE_LINK} from both builds, the usual one and the one that can have UI access, put in {$START_TAG_CODE}dist{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}:
translations.docs.build.setup.wrap: The setup that's published carries that installer and runs it silently, from a window of its own or, given Inno Setup's switches as WinGet and “Update app” give them, without one. It's built with the installer's absolute path in {$START_TAG_CODE}WINDICT_SETUP{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}:
translations.docs.build.contribute.title: Contributing
translations.docs.build.contribute.text: Bug reports and ideas are welcome as {$START_LINK}issues on GitHub{$CLOSE_LINK}.
translations.docs.dicts.title: Dictionaries and network use
translations.docs.dicts.lead: Where definitions and translations come from, and what WinDict sends over the network.
translations.docs.dicts.sources.title: The dictionaries
translations.docs.dicts.english: {$START_TAG_STRONG}English{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} comes from Open English WordNet, over 150,000 words and phrases, which is built into the executable. Lookups in it don't use the network and take under a millisecond.
translations.docs.dicts.italian: {$START_TAG_STRONG}Italian{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} comes from Wikizionario, about 67,000 words. It's downloaded once, about 8 MB, when it's chosen under {$START_TAG_STRONG}Languages{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} in the settings, and kept in {$START_TAG_CODE}%LOCALAPPDATA%\WinDict\dicts{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}.
translations.docs.dicts.online: The {$START_TAG_STRONG}online dictionary{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} is used for pronunciations and for words the built-in ones don't have: Wiktionary, through dictionaryapi.dev, and Wikizionario for Italian.
translations.docs.dicts.order: With both languages chosen, a word is looked up in them in the order they're listed, English first.
translations.docs.dicts.network.title: What goes over the network
translations.docs.dicts.network.lookup: A word you look up, to the online dictionary, only when the built-in one doesn't have it or for its pronunciation. Turn off {$START_TAG_STRONG}Online dictionary{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} in the settings to never send one.
translations.docs.dicts.network.translate: Text you translate, to Google Translate or MyMemory, only when you ask for a translation.
translations.docs.dicts.network.update: Once a day, a request to GitHub for the latest version. Turn off {$START_TAG_STRONG}Check for updates{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} to stop it.
translations.docs.dicts.network.cache: Answers are kept for a while, so asking again doesn't go over the network a second time.
translations.docs.dicts.memory.title: Memory
translations.docs.dicts.memory.text: WinDict uses about 4 MB of memory while idle. The dictionaries are read in place: Windows only loads the few parts a lookup touches.
translations.docs.dicts.credits.title: Credits
translations.docs.dicts.credits.wordnet: English definitions: {$START_LINK}Open English WordNet{$CLOSE_LINK} (CC BY 4.0, derived from Princeton WordNet).
translations.docs.dicts.credits.wiktionary: Online English lookups: {$START_LINK}Wiktionary{$CLOSE_LINK}, through {$START_LINK_1}dictionaryapi.dev{$CLOSE_LINK}, falling back to Wiktionary directly.
translations.docs.dicts.credits.wikizionario: Italian dictionary and online lookups: {$START_LINK}Wikizionario{$CLOSE_LINK}, through {$START_LINK_1}wiktextract{$CLOSE_LINK}, falling back to Wikizionario's own API (CC BY-SA 4.0).
translations.docs.dicts.credits.translate: Translations: Google Translate's public web endpoint, which is unofficial and may change, falling back to {$START_LINK}MyMemory{$CLOSE_LINK}.

translations.docs.start.title: Getting started
translations.docs.start.lead: Install WinDict, or run it without installing, and look up your first word.
translations.docs.start.requirements: WinDict runs on {$START_TAG_STRONG}Windows 10 and 11{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}. Older versions might work, but they aren't tested.
translations.docs.start.setup.title: Install with the setup (recommended)
translations.docs.start.setup.1: Download {$START_TAG_CODE}WinDict-<version>-setup.exe{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} from the {$START_LINK}latest release{$CLOSE_LINK} on GitHub.
translations.docs.start.setup.2: Run it, then choose {$START_TAG_STRONG}Install{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}. It installs WinDict for everyone on the PC, in {$START_TAG_CODE}C:\Program Files\WinDict{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, and adds it to Start and to Settings → Apps, where it can be uninstalled.
translations.docs.start.setup.3: Choose {$START_TAG_STRONG}Open WinDict{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}. A short introduction goes through the shortcuts, each with an example card.
translations.docs.start.setup.why: Only the installed copy can {$START_LINK}show the card above the Start menu{$CLOSE_LINK}, and it updates without asking for permission.
translations.docs.start.winget.title: Install with WinGet
translations.docs.start.winget.text: WinGet installs the same setup, from a terminal:
translations.docs.start.winget.upgrade: To update it the same way, use {$START_TAG_CODE}winget upgrade BosioPietro.WinDict{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, or {$START_TAG_STRONG}Update app{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} in WinDict's tray menu.
translations.docs.start.portable.title: Run it without installing
translations.docs.start.portable.text: Download {$START_TAG_CODE}WinDict-<version>.exe{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} instead and run it from anywhere: it's the whole app in a single executable. Its settings are kept in the same place as the installed copy's.
translations.docs.start.smartscreen.title: Windows says it protected your PC
translations.docs.start.smartscreen.text: WinDict isn't commercially signed, so the first time you run it, Windows SmartScreen may ask for confirmation. Choose {$START_TAG_STRONG}More info{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}, then {$START_TAG_STRONG}Run anyway{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}.
translations.docs.start.first.title: Your first lookup
translations.docs.start.first.text: Select a word in any app and press {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS}. Its definition opens in a card next to the selection. {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_1}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} or a click elsewhere closes it.
translations.home.hero.shotAlt: WinDict's card showing the definition of “gleam”, next to the word selected in an e-book
translations.docs.start.first.translate: To translate instead, select a word, a phrase or a passage and press {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS}.
translations.docs.start.tray.title: In the notification area
translations.docs.start.tray.text: While it runs, WinDict waits in the notification area, by the clock. Click its icon for its menu:
translations.docs.start.tray.autostart: {$START_TAG_STRONG}Start with Windows{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}, to run it when you sign in;
translations.docs.start.tray.update: {$START_TAG_STRONG}Update app{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}, when there's a new version: the icon shows a dot then;
translations.home.tray.shotAlt: WinDict's icon among the hidden icons of the Windows taskbar
translations.docs.start.uninstall.title: Uninstalling
translations.docs.start.uninstall.text: Uninstall the installed copy from Settings → Apps, like any other app. The copy that isn't installed is just its executable: quit it from the tray and delete it. Settings stay in {$START_TAG_CODE}%APPDATA%\WinDict{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, and downloaded dictionaries in {$START_TAG_CODE}%LOCALAPPDATA%\WinDict{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, should you want to remove them too.
translations.docs.lookup.title: Looking up words
translations.docs.lookup.lead: Select a word in any app and press {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS}: its definition opens in a card next to the selection.
translations.home.lookup.shotAlt: The definition of “gleam”: its senses as a verb and as a noun, with examples and similar words
translations.docs.lookup.card.title: What the card shows
translations.docs.lookup.card.text: The card lists the word's senses under each part of speech it can be, each with an example sentence where the dictionary has one. You can select a word or a short phrase, of up to four words.
translations.docs.lookup.card.forms: {$START_TAG_STRONG}Inflected forms{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} are looked up by their base word, so selecting “ran” shows “run”, and the card says what it's the form of.
translations.docs.lookup.card.similar: {$START_TAG_STRONG}Similar words{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} and, where there are any, {$START_TAG_STRONG}opposite{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} ones (“good”: “bad”) are listed under each part of speech. Clicking one opens its definition in the same card.
translations.docs.lookup.card.back: To go back, use the arrow next to the word, {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS}, {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_1}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} or the mouse's back button.
translations.docs.lookup.card.spelling: When a word isn't in the dictionary, the card suggests the closest one it has: “Did you mean…?”
translations.docs.lookup.speak.title: Hearing a word
translations.docs.lookup.speak.text: The speaker button after the word says it out loud, in the word's own language, with a voice Windows has for it. It shows only when there's one: voices for more languages can be added in Windows Settings, under Time & language → Speech.
translations.docs.lookup.type.title: Typing a word
translations.docs.lookup.type.text: With nothing selected, {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} opens a box to type a word into instead, for text that can't be selected, such as in an image, a protected PDF or a game.
translations.docs.lookup.type.suggest: As you type, up to five suggestions from the offline dictionary appear under the box. Pick one with {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} or {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_1}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS}, or click it.
translations.docs.lookup.type.enter: {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} looks up what's in the box. When the offline dictionary has nothing like it, Enter searches online.
translations.docs.lookup.pin.title: Pinning a card
translations.docs.lookup.pin.text: The pin button at the top right of the card keeps it open. A pinned card stays above every other window until you close it, and you can drag it wherever you like. New lookups open cards of their own, so you can keep several pinned side by side.
translations.docs.lookup.pin.close: Once you've clicked a pinned card, it takes the keyboard like any window: {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} or {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_1}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} closes it, and the card's other keys work as usual. The pin button unpins it again.
translations.docs.lookup.copy.title: Copying
translations.docs.lookup.copy.text: {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} on a card copies the word, or the translation when it shows one. With a similar word picked with {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_1}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS}, it copies that word instead.
translations.docs.lookup.size.title: Text size
translations.docs.lookup.size.text: To make the card's text larger or smaller, press {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} or {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_1}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS}, or hold {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_2}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} and turn the mouse wheel over the card. {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_3}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} goes back to the usual size. The size goes from 80% to 200%, is kept, and is also under {$START_TAG_STRONG}Text size{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} in the settings. The settings window follows the same size, and the same keys work there.
translations.docs.lookup.reading.title: How WinDict reads the selection
translations.docs.lookup.reading.text: WinDict reads the selection through UI Automation, the way screen readers do, so nothing is copied and the clipboard isn't touched. Some apps don't share their text that way: for those, choose {$START_TAG_STRONG}Automatic{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} under {$START_TAG_STRONG}Read selections{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} in the settings, and WinDict copies the selection there instead, then puts back what was on the clipboard. See {$START_LINK}Settings{$CLOSE_LINK}.
translations.docs.settings.title: Settings
translations.docs.settings.lead: Open the tray menu and choose {$START_TAG_STRONG}Settings…{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}. Changes apply right away.
translations.docs.settings.general.title: General
translations.docs.settings.autostart.text: Runs WinDict when you sign in. Also in the tray menu.
translations.docs.settings.aboveStart.text: Opens the card on top of Start and Search. Only in the installed copy: see {$START_LINK}Above the Start menu{$CLOSE_LINK}.
translations.docs.settings.updates.text: Once a day. When there's a new version, the tray icon shows a dot and its menu has {$START_TAG_STRONG}Update app{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}.
translations.docs.settings.language.text: The language WinDict is shown in: English or Italiano. At first, the language of Windows, if WinDict has it.
translations.docs.settings.shortcuts.text: The keys that look up and translate, {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} and {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_1}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} at first. Click one and press the new keys; {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_2}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} keeps the old ones.
translations.docs.settings.card.title: Card
translations.docs.settings.theme.text: System, Light or Dark. With System, the card follows Windows, and always takes its accent color.
translations.docs.settings.textSize.text: From 80% to 200%. Also {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS}, {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_1}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} or Ctrl and the mouse wheel on the card.
translations.docs.settings.definitions.text: Senses shown per part of speech, from 1 to 10. 4 at first.
translations.docs.settings.synonyms.text: Similar words under each part of speech, from 0, which hides them, to 12. 6 at first.
translations.docs.settings.examples.text: Sentences showing each sense in use.
translations.docs.settings.animations.text: At first as Windows has them, under Accessibility → Visual effects. Turn on or off to override it.
translations.docs.settings.lookup.title: Lookup
translations.docs.settings.online.text: For pronunciations, and words the built-in dictionaries lack. Translations need it on.
translations.docs.settings.languages.text: The dictionaries words are looked up in. English is built in; choosing Italiano downloads its dictionary, once.
translations.docs.settings.reading.title: Read selections
translations.docs.settings.reading.direct: {$START_TAG_STRONG}Direct only{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}, the default: reads the selection directly, through UI Automation. It opens faster, but misses selections in apps that can't be read that way. Switch to Automatic if words go missing.
translations.docs.settings.reading.automatic: {$START_TAG_STRONG}Automatic{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}: reads the selection directly, and copies it in apps where that isn't possible, putting back what was on the clipboard. Works in every app.
translations.docs.settings.reading.clipboard: {$START_TAG_STRONG}Clipboard only{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}: always copies the selection, which is slower. Try it if an app gives the wrong text.
translations.docs.settings.translation.title: Translation
translations.docs.settings.defaults.text: Translated from and into when the language can't be told: English into Italiano at first.
translations.docs.settings.email.text: Raises MyMemory's daily limit on free translations. It's sent only to MyMemory, with the text translated.
translations.docs.settings.file.title: The settings file
translations.docs.settings.file.text: The settings are stored in {$START_TAG_CODE}%APPDATA%\WinDict\config.json{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}. To edit the file by hand, use {$START_TAG_STRONG}Open config.json{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} at the bottom of the settings window, then {$START_TAG_STRONG}Reload settings{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} in the tray menu.
translations.docs.settings.file.keys: Shortcuts are written as in {$START_TAG_CODE}"Ctrl+Alt+D"{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} or {$START_TAG_CODE}"Win+Shift+F1"{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}: one key, with at least one of Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win.
translations.docs.keys.title: Keyboard shortcuts
translations.docs.keys.lead: Every key WinDict listens for, from anywhere in Windows and on the card.
translations.docs.keys.global.title: Anywhere in Windows
translations.docs.keys.global.text: These two work in every app. To change them, open {$START_TAG_STRONG}Shortcuts{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} under {$START_TAG_STRONG}General{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} in the settings, click the one to change and press the new keys; {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} keeps the old ones. A shortcut needs {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_1}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS}, {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_2}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} or {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_3}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} with its key.
translations.docs.keys.global.lookup: Looks up the selected word or phrase. With nothing selected, opens a box to type a word into.
translations.docs.keys.global.translate: Translates the selected text, up to 500 characters. With nothing selected, opens a box to type text into.
translations.docs.keys.card.title: On the card
translations.docs.keys.card.text: While a card is open, these keys act on it, without having to click it first.
translations.docs.keys.card.translate: Shows the word's translation, or its definition again
translations.docs.keys.card.copy: Copies the word, the translation, or the similar word picked with Tab
translations.docs.keys.card.back: Goes back to the word before. The mouse's back button does too.
translations.docs.keys.card.tab: Moves between the card's links and buttons
translations.docs.keys.card.enter: Opens the link or presses the button picked with Tab
translations.docs.keys.card.zoom: Makes the text larger or smaller. So does Ctrl with the mouse wheel.
translations.docs.keys.card.zoomReset: Goes back to the usual text size
translations.docs.keys.pinned.title: On a pinned card
translations.docs.keys.pinned.text: A pinned card takes the keyboard once you click it, like any other window. The keys above work there too, and:
translations.docs.keys.pinned.altf4: Closes it, as it closes any window
translations.docs.keys.box.title: In the box to type into
translations.docs.keys.box.enter: Looks up the word, or translates the text
translations.docs.keys.box.suggestions: Picks one of the suggestions under the box
translations.docs.keys.box.tab: Picks the next or the previous suggestion
translations.docs.keys.box.caret: Moves the caret, by words with Ctrl
translations.docs.keys.box.homeEnd: Moves the caret to the start or the end
translations.docs.keys.box.delete: Deletes before or after the caret, a word at a time with Ctrl
translations.docs.keys.picker.title: In the list of languages
translations.docs.keys.picker.text: When you click a language on a translation, type to filter the list.
translations.docs.keys.picker.move: Moves through the languages, as Tab and Shift+Tab do
translations.docs.keys.picker.page: Moves a page at a time
translations.docs.keys.menu.title: In the tray menu
translations.docs.keys.menu.ends: Goes to the first or the last item
translations.docs.translate.title: Translating
translations.docs.translate.lead: Translate a word, a phrase or a whole passage without leaving what you're reading.
translations.home.translate.shotAlt: “I'll keep you in the loop”, selected in an e-mail, translated into Italian in WinDict's card
translations.docs.translate.selection.title: Translating the selection
translations.docs.translate.selection.text: Select a word, a phrase or a whole passage, of up to 500 characters, and press {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS}: the card opens on the translation. For a single word the dictionary has, {$START_TAG_STRONG}Back{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} shows its definition.
translations.docs.translate.card.text: On a definition, the translate button at the top right of the card, or {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS}, shows a translation of the word instead. Press it again to go back to the definition.
translations.docs.translate.languages.text: The languages are at the top of the card. Click one to pick another, typing to filter the list, or the arrows between them to swap them.
translations.docs.translate.typing.title: Typing the text to translate
translations.docs.translate.typing.text: With nothing selected, {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} opens a box to type the text into, with the languages under it, as on the translation card. As you type, WinDict tells the language from its words, using the dictionaries you've chosen, and picks the languages:
translations.docs.translate.typing.two: with two dictionary languages, from the one you're typing in into the other;
translations.docs.translate.typing.defaults: otherwise, between the default languages in the settings, into the one you're not typing in;
translations.docs.translate.typing.unknown: when the language can't be told, the default way.
translations.docs.translate.typing.pick: Click a language to pick another one, or the arrows to swap them; from then on they stay as you set them. Press {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} to translate; Back on the translation brings the box back as you left it.
translations.docs.translate.list.title: Languages
translations.docs.translate.services.title: Where translations come from
translations.docs.translate.services.text: Translations come from Google Translate's public web endpoint, falling back to {$START_LINK}MyMemory{$CLOSE_LINK} when it can't answer. They need the online dictionary to be on, in the settings, and are fetched only when you ask for one.
translations.docs.translate.services.email: MyMemory has a daily limit on free translations. An e-mail address under {$START_TAG_STRONG}Translation → MyMemory email{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} in the settings raises it; it's sent only to MyMemory, with the text translated.
translations.home.hero.title: Any word, explained in place.
translations.home.hero.lead: Select a word in any app and press {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS}: its definition, or its translation, opens right beside it.
translations.home.hero.note: Free and open source · Windows 10 and 11
translations.home.lookup.title: Definitions, in any app
translations.home.lookup.text: Browsers, PDFs, e-mail, code editors: the card opens right under the word, and {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} or a click elsewhere closes it.
translations.home.lookup.point1.title: Offline, and instant
translations.home.lookup.point1: Over 150,000 English words and phrases from Open English WordNet are built in, so no connection is needed.
translations.home.lookup.point2.title: Every sense, with examples
translations.home.lookup.point2: Senses are grouped by part of speech, with example sentences and similar and opposite words a click away.
translations.home.lookup.point3.title: In Italian too
translations.home.lookup.point3: About 67,000 Italian words from Wikizionario, and an online dictionary for the words neither has.
translations.home.translate.title: Translate as you read
translations.home.translate.text: Select a word, a phrase or a whole passage and press {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS}. On a definition, {$START_TAG_APP_KEYS_1}{$CLOSE_TAG_APP_KEYS} translates the word.
translations.home.translate.point1.title: 22 languages
translations.home.translate.point1: From English and Italian to Japanese, Korean and Chinese.
translations.home.translate.point2.title: Languages picked for you
translations.home.translate.point2: WinDict tells the language from its words, and you can pick or swap them on the card.
translations.home.translate.point3.title: Whole passages
translations.home.translate.point3: Up to 500 characters at once, or type the text into a box when it can't be selected.
translations.home.start.title: Right on top of Start and Search
translations.home.start.text: Windows keeps Start and Search above every other window. Installed with its setup, WinDict can show the card on top of them too, so you can look up a word without leaving the Start menu.
translations.home.grid.title: Small, with everything you need
translations.home.grid.text: Written in Rust against the native Windows APIs, WinDict feels like part of Windows and costs next to nothing while it waits.
translations.home.keys.title: Two shortcuts to remember
translations.home.keys.text: Both can be changed in the settings. Everything else works from the keyboard too.
translations.home.keys.lookup.title: Look up
translations.home.keys.lookup.text: The selected word's definition, or a box to type one into.
translations.home.keys.translate.title: Translate
translations.home.keys.translate.text: The selected text's translation, or a box to type text into.
translations.home.tray.title: Up and running in a minute
translations.home.tray.step1.title: Download the setup
translations.home.tray.step1.text: From the latest release on GitHub, or with WinGet:
translations.home.tray.step2.title: Run it
translations.home.tray.step2.text: It installs WinDict for everyone on the PC and adds it to Start. A short introduction shows you around.
translations.home.tray.step3.title: Select a word, press Alt+D
translations.home.tray.step3.text: WinDict waits in the notification area, by the clock. Click its icon for the settings.
translations.home.faq.title: Questions and answers
translations.home.cta.title: Read without leaving the page
translations.home.cta.text: WinDict is free, open source, and about 4 MB of memory while it waits.
translations.home.stat.memory.label: of memory while idle
translations.home.stat.words.label: English words and phrases, offline
translations.home.stat.languages.label: languages to translate between
translations.home.stat.speed.label: for an offline lookup
translations.home.feature.pin.title: Pin a card
translations.home.feature.pin.text: Pin a definition and it stays on top of everything, wherever you drag it, while new lookups open cards of their own.
translations.home.feature.speak.title: Hear it said
translations.home.feature.speak.text: The speaker button says the word out loud in its own language, with the voices Windows already has.
translations.home.feature.similar.title: Similar and opposite words
translations.home.feature.similar.text: Each part of speech lists similar words and opposites. Click one to open it in the same card, then go back.
translations.home.feature.type.title: Type a word
translations.home.feature.type.text: With nothing selected, the shortcut opens a box to type into, with suggestions from the offline dictionary as you type.
translations.home.feature.forms.title: Base forms found for you
translations.home.feature.forms.text: Inflected forms are looked up by their base word, so “ran” shows “run”. Misspelled? The card asks what you meant.
translations.home.feature.theme.title: Your theme, your accent
translations.home.feature.theme.text: The card follows Windows' light or dark mode and accent color, on Mica-like acrylic, like the rest of the system.
translations.home.feature.size.title: Text the size you like
translations.home.feature.size.text: From 80% to 200%, with Ctrl+plus, Ctrl+minus or Ctrl and the mouse wheel. The size is remembered.
translations.home.feature.update.title: Updates itself
translations.home.feature.update.text: Once a day WinDict checks for a new version. When there is one, the tray icon shows a dot and the update is one click away.
translations.home.faq.free.a: Yes. WinDict is free and open source under the MIT license, with no ads, accounts or tracking.
translations.home.faq.smartscreen.q: Why does Windows warn me when I run it?
translations.home.faq.smartscreen.a: WinDict isn't commercially signed, so the first time SmartScreen may ask for confirmation. Choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.
translations.home.faq.offline.a: English definitions are built in and work without a connection. Italian works offline once its dictionary is downloaded. Translations, and words the built-in dictionaries don't have, need the internet.
translations.home.faq.network.q: What does it send over the network?
translations.home.faq.network.a: Only what you ask for: the word, when it's looked up online, and the text, when it's translated. WinDict also checks GitHub for a new version once a day. Both the online dictionary, which translations need, and the update check can be turned off in the settings.
translations.home.faq.languages.a: Definitions in English and Italian, translations between 22 languages, and the app itself in English and Italian.
translations.home.faq.windows.q: Which versions of Windows does it run on?
translations.home.faq.windows.a: Windows 10 and 11. Older versions might work, but they aren't tested.
translations.home.faq.portable.q: Do I have to install it?
translations.home.faq.portable.a: No. There's a single executable that runs from anywhere. Installing it with the setup adds it to Start and lets the card show above the Start menu.
translations.notFound.title: No definition found
translations.notFound.text: This page isn't in the dictionary. Check the spelling?
translations.seo.description: WinDict is a free Windows app for looking up and translating words: select a word in any app, press Alt+D, and its definition opens right next to it.
